# NetTango

> NetTango is a block-based programming interface for NetLogo agent-based models. Students assemble blocks that set the rules of a simulation and run it in the browser; teachers build block sets for new models with the NetTango Builder.

## Site

- [Home](https://tango.netlogo.org/): Overview of NetTango for teachers, with a running model and the topics covered.
- [Models Library](https://tango.netlogo.org/models-library): Every ready-to-run model, grouped by classroom topic.

## Models: Antomology

Six models in order, from 2 blocks to 13. Your students start with a single ant looking for food and build up to a full colony with pheromones, a life cycle and predators.

- [Antomology - Introduction](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/antomology-introduction): In this game, two colonies of ants forage for food. Though each ant follows a set of simple rules, the colonies as a whole act in sophisticated ways. Ant Adaptation simulates two ant colonies side by side, each controlled by a different player.
- [Antomology - Foraging For Food](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/antomology-foraging-for-food): In this game, two colonies of ants forage for food. Though each ant follows a set of simple rules, the colonies as a whole act in sophisticated ways. Ant Adaptation simulates two ant colonies side by side, each controlled by a different player.
- [Antomology - Ant Colony](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/antomology-ant-colony): In this game, two colonies of ants forage for food. Though each ant follows a set of simple rules, the colonies as a whole act in sophisticated ways. Ant Adaptation simulates two ant colonies side by side, each controlled by a different player.
- [Antomology - Pheromones](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/antomology-pheromones): In this game, two colonies of ants forage for food. Though each ant follows a set of simple rules, the colonies as a whole act in sophisticated ways. Ant Adaptation simulates two ant colonies side by side, each controlled by a different player.
- [Antomology - Life Cycle](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/antomology-life-cycle): In this game, two colonies of ants forage for food. Though each ant follows a set of simple rules, the colonies as a whole act in sophisticated ways. Ant Adaptation simulates two ant colonies side by side, each controlled by a different player.
- [Antomology - Predation](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/antomology-predation): In this game, two colonies of ants forage for food. Though each ant follows a set of simple rules, the colonies as a whole act in sophisticated ways. Ant Adaptation simulates two ant colonies side by side, each controlled by a different player.

## Models: Rollypollies

Two models in order. Your students write the rules one rollypolly follows, then run a class experiment on whether rollypollies gather in a dry chamber or a moist one.

- [Rollypollies Simple](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/rollypollies-simple): A NetTango blocks environment from the Biology collection.
- [Rollypollies](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/rollypollies): Rollypollies wander between a dry chamber and a moist one. Simple movement rules decide where the animals end up gathering.

## Models: Gases and particles

Your students program how gas particles move and collide, then use the pattern they see to explain gas behavior and heat transfer.

- [Two Particles in a Box](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/two-particle-sandbox): This model enables students to draw a model to "sketch" up representations of new systems to explore concepts related to gas behavior and gas particles. A wide range of real world systems can be modeled with this simple interface (e.g. diffusion of perfume from an uncapped container, hot gas mixed with a cold gas, mixtures of gases).
- [Ideal Gas Law](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/ideal-gas-law): This model enables students to draw a model to "sketch" up representations of new systems to explore concepts related to gas behavior and gas particles. A wide range of real world systems can be modeled with this simple interface (e.g. diffusion of perfume from an uncapped container, hot gas mixed with a cold gas, mixtures of gases).
- [Gas Particle Sandbox](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/gpc): Program how gas particles move, collide, and bounce off the walls of a sealed container, then watch the rules play out.
- [Particles Sandbox](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/particles-sandbox): This model supports a drawing style interface for "sketching" up representations of new systems to explore related to gas behavior and gas particles. This model is part of the "Connected Chemistry" curriculum http://ccl.northwestern.edu/curriculum/ConnectedChemistry/ which explores the behavior of gases.
- [Thermal Equilibration](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/thermal-equilibration): This model supports a drawing style interface for "sketching" up representations of new systems to explore related to gas behavior and gas particles. This model is part of the "Connected Chemistry" curriculum http://ccl.northwestern.edu/curriculum/ConnectedChemistry/ which explores the behavior of gases.

## Models: Spaceship programming

Two models in order. Your students schedule engine firings to fly a spaceship to a target, then set the force of each engine.

- [Spaceship Programming](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/spaceship-programming): Students schedule timed engine firings with blocks to fly a spaceship to a target. The ship keeps its velocity until an opposing engine fires.
- [Spaceship Programming: Variable Engines](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/spaceship-programming-variable-engines): Follows Spaceship Programming. Students again schedule engine firings with blocks to reach a target, and now set each engine's force from 0 to 10 N.

## Models: Disease spread

Two models in order. Your students build rules for how a disease spreads through a crowd and test what slows it down.

- [Simplified Disease](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/simplified-disease): A NetTango blocks environment from the Theory Building collection.
- [Disease](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/disease): A NetTango blocks environment from the Theory Building collection.

## Models: Biology

Your students build the rules one ant or one slime mold cell follows and watch a colony find food or the cells gather into clusters.

- [Ants](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/ants): A colony of ants forages for food and lays pheromone trails back to the nest. This is the finished project from the NetTango Builder tutorial.
- [Slime Tutorial](https://tango.netlogo.org/models/slime-tutorial): This model is inspired by the aggregation behavior of slime-mold cells. It is the final checkpoint of Jeremy Baker's NetTango Builder tutorial.

## Tutorials

- [Introduction to the NetTango Builder](https://tango.netlogo.org/tutorials/introduction-to-the-nettango-builder): Learn how to use the NetTango Builder to create a blocks-based programming interface for the NetLogo Ants model. This tutorial will guide you through the process of designing your own domain-specific blocks and connecting them to an existing NetLogo model.

## Builder

- [NetTango Builder](https://netlogoweb.org/nettango-builder): The web editor for designing block sets and attaching them to a NetLogo model; every model page links to it with its project file loaded.
